- Expected peak: ~6 concurrent sessions, 1k tokens/sec sustained during inference windows (models are a mix of 70B encoder-decoder + smaller rerankers)

- The 1k tokens/sec is an averaged number; in-burst windows we may see spikes to ~2k TPS for short (30–90s) periods during batch scoring.
- Model mix: primary model is a 70B transformer we intend to run at fp16 for pilot; later we may try a 4-bit quantized variant. Reranker is CPU-light but needs quick round-trips.
- Pilot start target: week of Oct 11 (hence the urgency on lead times).

We are open to a mixed approach if that helps control costs while meeting latency SLOs. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want specifics.

Thanks Sam — noted on the spike behavior. I've started the scenario mapping (attached) and summarized options below so the fleet planning meeting can make a quick decision. Attachment: NEB-4721_capacity_scenarios_v3.xlsx

Summary (pilot -> expansion):
- Conservative: 4 x A100-80GB reserved nodes + 1 burst pool (works at FP16; risk: 95th pct latency may exceed 250ms during bursts)
- Balanced (recommended): 6 x H100-80GB reserved (safety headroom for peaks) + small burst pool; allows headroom for quantized variants to reduce sustained unit cost
- Aggressive (fast expansion): 12 x H100 reserved + dedicated reranker pool (high cost, low lat risk)

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling lead time: 3–5 working days to seed dedicated H100 reserved capacity in target region (us-west).
- Caching: suggest enabling prefix KV caching for their repeated prompts — could cut token load by ~18% in our estimation for Nebula's traffic pattern.
- Fallbacks: provide a slightly smaller quantized model as automatic fallback if latency spikes or reserved queue saturates.

As requested, Ben — can you confirm which option we can commit to by Thursday's meeting and call out any infra blockers? Laura — please add a quick cost delta per option so we can present committed vs no-commit economics.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Ava / Team —

Quick infra readout after a capacity check:
- We can realistically commit to the Balanced option (6 x H100-80GB reserved in us-west) for the pilot start date (week of Oct 11) if procurement signs LOI by Oct 1. Lead time includes image bake + network setup.
- Risk: there are two large reserved requests already queued for the same week (enterprise commitments). If both land, our H100 availability will drop ~30% for that week — in that case we can serve Nebula via a mixed pool: 4 reserved H100 + 4 A100 reserved in a cross-sku pool with autoscaler rules pinned to latency thresholds. That solution adds ~12% cost but keeps 95th pct latency within SLA in our internal sims.
- Burst credits: available but insufficient alone for the expected peak bursts; not recommended as the only solution.

Action items I can own:
- Confirm final SKU/placement (H100 vs H100+A100 hybrid) by Wed 21 Sep after we reconcile queued reservations.
- Provide runbook for fallback to quantized model + autoscaler tuning (will attach to the Drive link).

Laura — please flag if the hybrid option needs pre-approval from finance for the cost delta.

Ben
